{"title":"Plan: 5 days in Lisbon","parentId":"LRvZLVSbZeWOZWU14lvBS","icon":"🇵🇹","markdown":"Five days in Lisbon in late spring — part holiday, part scouting trip for a longer stay next year. Base in Graça throughout; times are intentions, not contracts.

## Day 1 — Arrive and settle into Alfama

Arrive Thursday morning, get to the Graça apartment, and settle in without rushing. Spend the afternoon wandering Alfama — the old maze below the castle, where getting lost on purpose is the point. Keep the evening easy: a tasca dinner, or Time Out Market if you go early.

## Day 2 — Castle, tram, and fado

Start at Castelo de São Jorge in the morning, then ride Tram 28 end to end (day passes for two: €14). In the evening, head back into Alfama for fado with supper (€100 for two).

## Day 3 — Belém and pastéis

Morning in Belém for the monastery and tower, then Pastéis de Belém — warm, with cinnamon, from the original bakery. The Lisboa Card only pays off if you do two paid museums today. Finish with sunset at Miradouro da Graça.

Don't miss the neighbourhood tasca in Graça for grilled sardines (€85 for two on Saturday), and a standing shot at a ginjinha stand at some point today or tomorrow.

## Day 4 — Sintra day trip

If the weather holds, take the train to Sintra. Book Pena Palace for the first slot — it fills up by 11 (tickets for two: €40) — then visit Quinta da Regaleira in the afternoon. Train back in the evening for Bairro Alto.

## Day 5 — LX Factory and home

Slow morning at LX Factory, then souvenirs and a last coffee — leave room in the bag for tins of sardines and ceramics. Fly home Monday evening.

Useful links: the day-by-day table is in [Lisbon itinerary](/p/qYHLnUAS1Djw1oCkHYFZf), food and neighbourhoods in [Lisbon food & neighbourhoods](/p/e6dEPOOJ6SQBdb2KQPsme), and bookings in [Packing & logistics](/p/_rw918YD5abm_TQ9Jc2bF).
"}

toolCalls.arguments:
{"title":"Reading notes — summary","markdown":"A summary of [Reading notes](/p/KMmPdOmftQxlYF-TBmBf6), which holds notes on books actually finished — two so far this year. Notes are written from memory a week after finishing, and a book only gets a page if it changed how the reader does something.

## [The Design of Everyday Things](/p/omtbu_iXZfD8_qBU4-tUv) — Don Norman

- **Affordances vs signifiers:** what an object *can* do vs what it *tells* you it can do. Most "user error" is missing signifiers.
- **Norman doors:** if a door needs a push/pull sign, the door failed, not the person.
- **Feedback:** every action needs a visible result, immediately, or people repeat it.
- **Constraints** are kindness: make the wrong thing impossible instead of warning about it.

Application: product onboarding reviews — every "users keep doing X wrong" is treated as a signifier bug until proven otherwise.

## [Thinking in Systems](/p/n8Y4gqu6FTmAATBkY7mxb) — Donella Meadows

- **Stocks and flows:** you can only change a stock through its flows, and flows are usually slow. Patience is a strategy.
- **Feedback loops:** reinforcing loops explain runaway growth and collapse; balancing loops explain stubborn plateaus.
- **Leverage points:** changing goals and paradigms beats tweaking parameters — but it's the hardest place to push.
- **Bounded rationality:** every actor is rational inside their own information bubble. Fix the information, not the actor.

> "We can't control systems or figure them out. But we can dance with them."

Application: when a metric won't move, the reader checks whether they're pushing a parameter when the goal of the system is the problem.

## How the two connect

The notes cross-reference each other: the design lens from Norman pairs with the systems view in Meadows, and the systems lens is likewise read alongside Norman's design ideas.","parentId":"KMmPdOmftQxlYF-TBmBf6","icon":"📚"}

{"title":"Job post: Full-stack engineer","parentId":"aqiGFuc3Eyrp74AcubIIy","icon":"💼","markdown":"## Full-stack engineer

*Draft — ready to publish once the placeholders below are filled in and the full-stack scorecard is agreed.*

### About the role

We're hiring a full-stack engineer as one of two roles that unblock our launch plan. This is a role hired for the next 18 months of problems, not the last 18 days — we're looking for someone who wants to own meaningful parts of the product and help shape where they go next.

### What you'll own

- **Billing** — own our billing work end to end, from the Product roadmap.
- **Public API** — own the public API, also from the Product roadmap.

These aren't side projects: billing and the public API are core to the launch, and you'll be the person responsible for them.

### What you'll do

- Build, ship, and maintain the billing and public API areas you own.
- Bring strong product sense to your work — weighing what to build, not just how to build it.
- Talk to pilot teams weekly, hear directly how they're using the product, and let that shape your decisions.

### Who we're looking for

- A full-stack engineer with strong product sense.
- Someone who enjoys regular contact with the teams using what they build, and uses those conversations to prioritise and improve their work.
- Someone excited by ownership of billing and the public API over the longer term.

*Further criteria will be set out in the agreed full-stack scorecard before this role opens.*

### How we hire

Our loop for this role:

1. **Work sample**
2. **Pairing session**
3. **Founder chat**

Every finalist also does a **paid work trial** — no role here is hired without one.

### Details to confirm before publishing

- [ ] Location / working arrangement: *[not yet specified]*
- [ ] Salary / compensation: *[not yet specified]*
- [ ] Benefits: *[not yet specified]*
- [ ] Tech stack: *[not yet specified]*
- [ ] Experience expected: *[not yet specified]*
- [ ] How to apply: *[not yet specified]*
- [ ] Full-stack scorecard agreed
"}
